name: Medical Devices and MedTech
blurb: AI medical devices, FDA authorization pathways, change control plans and device quality.
title: Medical Devices and MedTech
answer: The FDA keeps a public list of AI enabled medical devices it has authorized, now well over a thousand, most of them in radiology and most cleared through the 510(k) pathway. Its final guidance on predetermined change control plans lets makers get approval in advance for planned model updates, and in Europe AI devices also fall under the AI Act's high risk rules.

reading.body:
The FDA's list of authorized AI medical devices has passed a thousand, and the approval regime now has a mechanism for updating models without starting over.

The pattern is regulatory catch-up. Most of those authorizations are radiology tools cleared through 510(k), a pathway built for devices that do not change. Predetermined change control plans, finalized in December 2024 and widened from machine learning devices to all AI enabled devices, let a maker get advance approval for planned model updates. That matters because retraining is continuous and a fresh submission per version is not viable. In Europe the same device must satisfy MDR or IVDR and, since August 2024, the AI Act, which classes devices needing notified body review as high risk.

For AI specifically, the constraint is not the model but the permission to change it. A device that cannot be updated decays in place, and the compute behind it is irrelevant if the update cannot be cleared. The practical consequence is that change control gets designed at first submission, not after.

What this does not cover: the data gives no counts by year, no breakdown beyond radiology's majority, no recall or post-market outcomes, and no detail on how generative or large language model devices are treated. It also says nothing about compute, data centers, or power, which do not appear in this material at all.

sections.body: Plan model updates before the first submission: a change control plan agreed with the FDA is far cheaper than a new submission for every retraining. In Europe, budget for AI Act conformity alongside MDR, because the two now apply together.

developments.text: The FDA's public list of AI enabled medical devices passed one thousand authorizations, with radiology accounting for the large majority and nearly all cleared through the 510(k) pathway.
The EU AI Act entered into force, classing AI medical devices that need notified body review under MDR or IVDR as high risk AI systems.
